cards.explanation: The answer is that they keep away from any brother who leads an undisciplined life. Paul commands this in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, friends, and he calls it a life "…not in keeping with the tradition you received from us." (2 Thessalonians 3:6). Nothing in the verse is about questions or travel. It's about how a person is living.

The answer is False. Paul says they did not eat anyone's food without paying for it (2 Thessalonians 3:8). No freebies, friends, no tabs left behind. They covered their own meals while they were with the church.

The answer is burden. Paul says they worked "…night and day so that we would not be a burden to any of you." (2 Thessalonians 3:8). That's the whole reason for the long hours, friends. They didn't want to weigh on the church.

The answer is to be an example to imitate. Paul says they had the right to support, "…but we wanted to offer ourselves as an example for you to imitate." (2 Thessalonians 3:9). They had the right and chose to work anyway, friends. Talk is cheap, so they showed it with their own hands.

The answer is that anyone unwilling to work shall not eat. Paul says the command was given even while they were there: "If anyone is unwilling to work, he shall not eat." (2 Thessalonians 3:10). Notice it's about being unwilling, friends. That's a different thing from being unable. It's a short command, and it's easy to remember.

The answer is True. Paul writes, "For we hear that some of you are leading undisciplined lives, accomplishing nothing, but being busybodies." (2 Thessalonians 3:11). Accomplishing nothing is right there in the verse, friends. He says it straight, no sprinkles on top, and it's only some of them.

The answer is quietly. Paul commands and urges them "…to begin working quietly to earn their own living." (2 Thessalonians 3:12). Remember the busybodies from the verse before, friends. Quiet work is the other direction from that. And it comes by the Lord Jesus Christ.

The answer is don't get tired of doing good. Here Paul speaks to the brothers: "But as for you, brothers, do not grow weary in well-doing." (2 Thessalonians 3:13). Well-doing is the work, friends, and he's telling them not to wear out on it. Keep going.

The answer is as a brother to admonish. Paul says, "…do not regard him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother." (2 Thessalonians 3:15). The distance is real, friends, but so is the family tie. He's still a brother.

The answer is False. Paul writes, "…may the Lord of peace Himself give you peace at all times and in every way." (2 Thessalonians 3:16). There's no limit to hard times, friends. At all times means all times.

The answer is True. Paul writes, "This greeting is in my own hand…" and "This is my mark in every letter; it is the way I write." (2 Thessalonians 3:17). It's how the church could recognize a letter from him, friends. Right there in the verse.
